task.description: Implement REQ-166 strictly per the APPROVED design at lib/letflow/design/req166-wasm-module-abi-validation.md (passed CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR after one rework round, commit fa9cb17). Read the full design doc before writing any code -- it is unusually detailed and precise about the two-stage validation flow; follow it exactly rather than improvising. This environment has Rust 1.97.1 and wasmex's native NIF already built -- use export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" and WASMEX_BUILD=true for wasmex-touching mix commands. Steps: (1) Create lib/letflow/engine/wasm/module_registry.ex implementing Letflow.Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistry per design section 3 exactly: the @opaque RegisteredModule struct, register/1's two-stage flow (design section 5.1) -- stage 1 static export/signature check via Wasmex.Store.new/0 + Wasmex.Module.compile/2 + Wasmex.Module.exports/1 against the exact required-export table in section 5.2, collecting ALL defects not stopping at first; stage 2 (only if stage 1 found zero defects) a real instantiation attempt via Wasmex.start_link/1 run INSIDE a Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2 task (never inline -- this is load-bearing per the design's own live-reproduced crash-propagation finding in section 1.5) under a NEW dedicated Letflow.Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor, read back via Task.yield/2 with a bounded timeout, branching on the outcome per section 5.1 step 7 exactly (success -> GenServer.stop the instance then return {:ok, registered_module()}; {:exit, reason} matching the unresolved-import pattern -> {:error, {:instantiation_failed, {:unresolved_import, namespace, function}}}; any other crash shape -> {:crashed, raw_reason}; timeout -> Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) then {:timeout, timeout_ms}). (2) Add the new Task.Supervisor child spec to lib/letflow/application.ex's supervision tree (design section 2.2) -- this is the one file outside module_registry.ex this design touches. (3) Write the moduledoc content per design section 2.3 (WASM-02 restatement, req163 section 3.1/3.2/4 citations, the two-stage gate description). Do NOT modify lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex or lib/letflow/engine/plugin_interface.ex -- both are explicitly out of scope per design section 2.1 (registration is fully decoupled from invocation in this requirement).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: a test registers a module missing the execute export and asserts registration fails with {:error, {:invalid_abi, defects}} naming {:missing, "execute"} among the defects.

AC2: a test asserts a module missing EACH of the other 5 required exports (init, deinit, get_capabilities, alloc, memory) is likewise rejected -- one test case per required export, plus at least one test asserting multiple simultaneous missing exports all appear in the defects list (design section 5.1 step 5's collect-all-not-stop-on-first requirement).

AC3: a test asserts rejection happens at REGISTRATION and not at invocation -- a non-conforming module never produces a registered_module() value, and (per the opaque type) no test can construct one to feed into an invocation path; also test the NEW stage-2 rejection case -- a module with all 5 exports correctly shaped but an unresolved WASI import is rejected with {:error, {:instantiation_failed, {:unresolved_import, namespace, function}}}, proving req163 section 4's instantiation-based rejection is genuinely wired in.

AC4: a test asserts a conforming module (all exports correct AND no unresolved imports) registers successfully with {:ok, registered_module()}, and that the instantiation-proving Wasmex instance is stopped (not leaked) before register/1 returns (mirror REQ-165's own leak-detection test technique from test/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler_test.exs).
AC5: the moduledoc names the export contract and cites req163-wasm-abi-choice.md as its source (sections 3.1/3.2 for the contract, section 4 for the instantiation-rejection requirement).
AC6: mix test and mix compile --warnings-as-errors both pass, real output quoted.

Additional (from design's own rigor, not a numbered AC but required by the design you're implementing): a test asserts that calling register/1 on an unresolved-import module does NOT crash the calling test process (proving the Task.Supervisor wrapping actually works, mirroring the design's own section 1.5 live reproduction) -- this is the single most important test given the entire design's central fix was this exact crash-propagation hazard.
